.WHAT HAS CHANGED...

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 226 AM EDT Monday...

1. Mostly dry weather will continue through Tuesday.

2. More widespread precipitation is expected to arrive 
Wednesday night into Thursday.   

3. High pressure will bring a spell of drier weather to the 
region late week into the weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 226 AM EDT Monday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: An upper low remains centered over the Canadian 
Maritimes to our east, with high pressure building into the region 
bringing dry and seasonable conditions for the first portion of the 
week. Temperatures today will climb into the 70s across the region 
with some mostly sunny skies. A decaying cold front pushing through 
Monday night into early Tuesday may bring spark some light rain 
showers, particularly near the Canadian border, although this 
feature may lead to increased cloud cover rather than any actual 
precipitation. Tuesday looks to be another dry and seasonably cool 
day, with highs in the upper 60s to mid 70s.

KEY MESSAGE 2: As we head into the middle of the week, a series of 
frontal boundaries will bring chances of widespread precipitation 
for Wednesday night into Thursday. A plume of tropical moisture will 
advect into the region, with PWAT values in excess of 2 inches, 
allowing for a period of moderate to heavy rainfall. Fast flow aloft 
and a decent LLJ will keep the system moving, limiting the duration 
of any heavy rainfall. Additionally, limited instability and weak 
mid-level lapse rates will limit convective potential, with mostly 
beneficial rainfall expected and any hydrological concerns unlikely. 
At this time rainfall amounts look to generally range between 0.25 
and 0.75 inches, although some amounts closer to an inch may be 
possible, especially with any orographic enhancement, but as we get 
closer more detail is expected. While the bulk of precipitation is 
expected Wednesday night into Thursday morning, a few diurnally 
driven showers will be possible throughout the day Thursday, 
especially across the high terrain with lingering moisture.

KEY MESSAGE 3: Following the frontal passage on Thursday, high pressure 
will quickly establish itself across the North Country on Friday. 
Plenty of sunshine, light winds, and drier weather will ensue once 
the high pressure system builds overhead. This will likely set up a 
classic fog situation Friday night and Saturday night with 
widespread dense fog across the river valleys of Vermont and 
northern New York. We could see some rain chances as early as 
Sunday afternoon as the deterministic guidance is split on how much 
a shortwave will dig out an upper level trough across the Great 
Lakes region. The most likely scenario is little to no shower 
activity on Sunday and at worst case scenario a weak front will 
bring scattered rain chances. Either way, it'll be a nice end of the 
work week and weekend across the region. The upper level pattern 
becomes more amplified towards the beginning of next week which 
could potentially introduce some rain chances but if the 
amplification occurs across the Rockies, it may act to enhance the 
upper level ridge and bring an extended period of dry weather to the 
North Country.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Through 06Z Tuesday...VFR conditions will prevail through most
of the period under mostly clear skies. Some patchy dense fog
and/or a low stratus deck is expected to develop across the
favorable river valleys which may introduce a brief period of
IFR fog at KSLK, KMPV, and KEFK between 8Z and 12Z. Otherwise,
light winds this morning will become northerly at 8 to 15 knots
by late morning and go light and variable once again tonight.

Outlook...

SHRA, Slight chance TSRA.
Thursday: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Thursday Night: VFR. Slight chance SHRA.
Friday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
